Ready for the maintainer to merge.

## What looks good

- The switch is read in one place (`operation::planner_switch`) and enforced at the kind level: under `CAMCRAFT_PLANNER=new` only the 2D Pocket passes `check_engine` (`KERNEL_KINDS = [Pocket]`, `planner_switch.rs`); every other phase-1 kind is refused by name with the escape text ("unset CAMCRAFT_PLANNER or set it to \"old\""). There is no silent fallback: the Pocket arm either takes the kernel route or returns the refusal `?`.
- The recipe refuses what it does not plan, each by name: Adaptive (`KERNEL_POCKET_ADAPTIVE`), Zigzag (`KERNEL_POCKET_ZIGZAG`, #3753), rest machining and "do not touch" areas (`pocket_kernel.rs`, #3753/#3754) and the corner relief - with `unset CAMCRAFT_PLANNER` in each text. A closed pocket without a safe entry is refused by name (`NO_SAFE_ENTRY`, #4324). The old route is unchanged and the default is the default.
- The body tables are in the pins as measured. Old pins (`laws_pockets::pocket_2d_readings_of_the_old_planner`) are unchanged and both pins (old and kernel) are strict string equality. The fig8 rows (Auto 27996 moves, 6 crossings, 18 lifts named 18, air 6 / col 0 / solid 15, over 8595 worst 180 full 4179, breaks link L4 L6; Inside refused by name; Outside 7573 old / 27996 new, 18 lifts named 18, same reads) match a run of the heavy test exactly.
- The converter change is tight: `LevelPlan::top_z` (`None` = the stock top), `set_top` refuses a level top that is not finite or is above the stock top (`BAD_LEVEL_TOP`), and the entry check runs against the proved level top, not the stock top (`APPROACH_IN_MATERIAL`). Both refusals have tests.
- `without_slivers` (`kernel_region.rs`) drops only a loop whose area is below `SLIVER_WIDTH` (1e-4 mm) times its perimeter - i.e. a loop of no material - and keeps everything else; the pin test (`kernel_pocket_selection_drops_a_sliver_loop`) passes and the sliver-drop is the only change to the selection path.
- No pin was made weaker: the planner_switch test is strengthened (2D Pocket now passes `Ok(())` under `new`, with the old kinds still refused), the heavy/light pins check named lifts and counts on this head as measured, and the L7 record self-reference is documented in the module doc as deliberate.
- Provenance comments on the new modules, a decision record (`docs/decisions/3752-kernel-pocket-recipe.md`), no new dependencies, no snapshots touched, no process files touched.

## Results (local build in the review worktree; not on the runner)

The PR targets the `side/path-kernel` base (it is a sub-PR on that branch, not a fork PR), and the pr-test workflow would compute its read-only check against the merge-base with main, which is the unmerged branch - so it would refuse this PR as "read, not built". I built locally, per its own gate law (quick gate vs `origin/side/path-kernel`).

- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws` (registry, L1-L7 on the registered 2D Pocket): 163 passed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws` (`k6_pocket.rs`): 38 passed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test pocket_pass_start -- kernel_route`: 3 passed, 2 ignored (heavy/light)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start -- planner_switch`: 2 passed, 1 ignored
- Targeted heavy step (P1 under the safety floor): `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named` (+ its light twin) run directly: 2 passed (392 s)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-pathkernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): 7 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (22.2 min wall)
- Example catalog (default switch): `catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket`, `catalog_2d_edge_work`, `catalog_2d_first_part` - 4 passed; the 2 adaptive-pocket tests are the pre-existing heavy-lane ignore (#3163), not this PR

## Targeted tests

- The example catalog suites ran (default switch; the old planner is what the catalog exercises): 4 passed
- The light lane: 7 steps, 0 failed (22.2 min), including `app light: pocket_pass_start` (`fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named_light`)
- The targeted heavy step of this P1 (`app heavy: pocket_pass_start`): the author's result, and my own run of both tests of it, are green (2 passed).

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- Six `Crossing` findings on fig8 (2 per level, #4300) block the post under `new` - that is the honest state of the recipe, and it is named in the PR body: `kernel_route_pocket_generates_verifies_and_posts` pins a closed pocket that posts with the Fanuc post, and the fig8 pocket does not post until #4300 closes. The default stays the old planner, so this is opt-in.
- The open items (#4260, #4272: full-width and over-limit reads on Outside at the stock edge; #4300: crossings; #4324: the Inside refusal) are named in the body and tracked in issues; I did not re-check their text against this head beyond the table rows.
- The heavy/light pins (`kernel_route::fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named`, `offset_pass_start::planner_switch`'s ignored `switch_default_is_the_old_planner`) do not assert the 6-crossing count or the exact refusal reason text beyond the prefix; the refusal text is pinned in the pin of `kernel_route_refuses_what_the_recipe_does_not_plan`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
